# Results
Currently, I've only run the 'restricted' breeding strategy with the 'name' sensing information. We don't get quite as good results as they do in the paper -- they get down to **1.33** for name based and restricted breeding, but we only down to about **1.8** or so. It's very possible this is due to some small bug or misimplementation; certainly, we can see the results in an interesting fashion.

## Results
Currently just testing out the code for the results. Running on extremely small datasets for now. 

```{python}
def plot_loss_curves(clone_data, free_data, restricted_data, title):
    breeding_strategies = ["Clone", "Free", "Restricted"]
    data_list = [clone_data, free_data, restricted_data]
    colors = {"Clone": "steelblue", "Free": "darkorange", "Restricted": "seagreen"}
    n = len(clone_data["avg_loss"])
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=2)
    avg_ax, best_ax = axes

    for ax in axes:
        ax.set(ylim=(0, 6))

    for strategy, data in zip(breeding_strategies, data_list):
        avg_ax.plot(range(n), data["avg_loss"], label=strategy, color=colors[strategy])
        best_ax.plot(
            range(n), data["best_loss"], label=strategy, color=colors[strategy]
        )

    avg_ax.legend()
    best_ax.legend()
    avg_ax.set_title("Average Loss")
    best_ax.set_title("Best Loss")
    plt.title(title)
    return fig
```



```{python}
sensing_terminals = ["Name", "Deitic", "Base"]
"results/Restricted/Name/2026-04-02_checkpoint.npz"
timestamp = "2026-04-02"


for terminal in sensing_terminals:
  clone_data = np.load(Path("results") / terminal / "Clone" /  f"{timestamp}_checkpoint.npz")
  free_data  = np.load(Path("results") / terminal / "Free" /  f"{timestamp}_checkpoint.npz")
  restricted_data = np.load(Path("results") / terminal / "Restricted" /  f"{timestamp}_checkpoint.npz")
  plot_loss_curves(clone_data, free_data, restricted_data, title=terminal)
```
